lesson.grammar_point: reported speech for meetings and follow-ups

listenings.text: Most follow-up emails after a conference fail, and they fail for the same reason every time. They are about the sender. It was a pleasure to meet you. I would love to explore synergies. Please find attached our company overview. Nothing in any of those sentences could only have been written to one specific person, which means the reader has no idea whether you remember them at all. The email that works does the opposite. It quotes something the other person said, in their words, so they know you were listening. It names one thing you are going to do, and when. And it ends. Three lines. I have never once thought a follow-up email was too short, and I read about forty of them after every event.

There is a habit I have that people find strange until they try it. On the way out of a meeting, before I get to the lift, I record a voice note to myself and I use the person's own words. She said that the pilot would be ready by the first quarter. He told me that compliance was their main concern, not the price. They mentioned that the second corridor had not been approved yet. Two things happen. The obvious one is that I do not forget. The less obvious one, and the reason I really do it, is that reporting somebody's words back accurately is what makes the next conversation easy. If I open with what you told me last time, we are already inside the subject, and nobody has to spend ten minutes rebuilding where we were.

Voice note, Thursday, after the Northgate call. So, three things. She said that the integration would take twelve weeks in the good case, and she admitted that sixteen was more realistic for a bank with our number of systems. She also mentioned that they had done exactly this with a bank in Colombia last year, and she offered to introduce me to the person who ran it, which is the single most useful thing anybody has offered me all month. And the third one. I asked about the compliance side and she told me she did not have the answer, that her head of delivery owned it, and that she would come back to me by Tuesday. It is now Thursday and she has not. So the action item is mine: I will chase it in the morning and, if I hear nothing, I escalate.
